content.comment_body: Hello, I've managed to configure the HMI using [product_name] V16 to communicate with [product_name] for several functions, but I'm unable to display the correct date and time from [product_name] on the HMI. I'm using date and time information as a template for the screens. Could anyone offer guidance to help with this?

[product_name] does not provide date and time in the VM area as formatted strings like "hh: mm: ss" or "mm: dd: yyyy"; instead, they're supplied as individual byte-wise variables. If you set up separate input/output fields for each byte variable on the HMI, you'll be able to both display and modify date and time values directly from the HMI.
I've attached an example. The communication setup is all done within [product_name]. There's nothing else needed in [product_name]—the HMI independently reads and writes all variables.
After extraction, how should I open the attached files?
You mentioned you're working with [product_name] V16. My attachment is a V16 project file in Zip format.
I uploaded your program to the HMI, but it still doesn't show the correct date and time. The template error is: "the process tag is missing".
I don't have the HMI device; I can only test with the simulation tool. The simulation works, as shown in the attached screen recording.
I've resolved the issue—I just needed to configure the time server in the HMI. Thanks for your help.
Is your problem resolved now? Which time server are you referring to?
I set [product_name] as the time server in the HMI according to the instructions.
I'm not sure how the correct HMI time is connected to displaying the date/time from [product_name] on the HMI.

I configured the NTP settings of [product_name] to act as the time server and enabled "synchronization with time server" in the HMI, using [product_name]'s IP address. It looks like it can be set up in [product_name] configuration too, but I couldn't find a method for doing this with [product_name]. Anyway, it's working now and seems less complicated than other approaches.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users faced challenges syncing date and time information from the [product_name] device to the HMI through [product_name] V16. Main issues included representing time/date as byte variables, configuring HMI process tags, and establishing the HMI to use [product_name] as its time server. These setup difficulties initially prevented successful synchronization, but after following advice on proper configuration, users managed to resolve the issue.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a straightforward method to show the date and time from [product_name] on the HMI with proper formatting and real-time syncing, using [product_name] V16.
